model.formula: N=N0*(1+effectiveEfficiency)^n; effectiveEfficiency=0 under shared inhibition, otherwise e; ideal e=1 gives N0*2^n. positiveAdded=positiveCopies-2; positiveAmplified=(n>0 and positiveAdded>0); controlsValid=(blankCopies==0 and positiveAmplified)

parameters.positive initial: 2 existing target copies; counted separately from new copies
parameters.inhibition: Effective efficiency 0; existing sample/positive templates retained

assumptions: Selected target with suitable complementary primers and polymerase; perfect target specificity in this teaching model
Constant efficiency; no resource depletion, stochastic sampling, instrument signal, detection threshold or plateau
Contaminated scenario adds one target copy to blank; shared inhibition blocks copying without deleting any existing template
Positive starts with two copies; fractional outputs are expected quantities. Two inhibited targets at cycles0/1/2/3/4 stay2/2/2/2/2, with zero added
Control validity is separate from copies: no target in blank and actual positive increase after at least one cycle. Zero cycles or zero efficiency cannot verify amplification
limits: Not a protocol, diagnostic test or real detection probability; no real primers, temperatures or timings
Successful ordinary positive cannot exclude sample-specific inhibition
Copy quantities are not instrument signals. A failed real positive amplification signal does not imply DNA disappearance; real non-detection is not absence
Real abnormal blank signals may also involve non-specific amplification; model contamination is idealised target contamination
